content.comment_body: Dear [product_name] programmers, I have a program using two [product_name] modules in a master-slave setup, which generally works well, but I’ve run into a network issue. I want to switch to a master-master configuration instead. The problem with master-slave is that when the router and fiber converter stopped working, only the master continued, while the slave stopped—this caused major issues. Is there a bit or byte that could help detect this situation? When building the master-master setup (so the modules work even without LAN), I’m stuck on programming the connection signals. I've tried the example program but don't fully understand how the VB/VM bits function. I need to transmit four contacts back and forth between the two masters. Also, why doesn’t the simulation program show a network input as a button? If anyone could share an example of how to transfer a marker from master1 to master2 and vice versa, I’d appreciate it. I'd prefer the master-master configuration to allow a marker that indicates when a module shuts down unexpectedly. Thanks!
Hello, Please check the attached PDF, sourced from [product_name] application examples. Regards,

Thank you, but I already have those documents. My issue is that I can’t get it to work! In online monitoring, I don’t see the buttons—only the connection lines light up. I'm only using button inputs, not analog ones. It’s unclear why there isn’t an example program demonstrating this with basic button inputs.
Hello, Perhaps this thread containing an example may be useful: [article_no] networking. Regards,

Hi, Essentially, you can use the diagnostic features to spot network problems. For program diagnostics, select a digital network input and enable diagnostics, then integrate the logic as needed. At the device, you can configure the display to show diagnostic information when issues arise, or access the diagnostic menu for further details. Hope this helps.

Thanks for your advice. For now, the setup still runs on master-slave. I'll test additional settings this weekend. EDIT: It works! I had an addressing mistake in the client reading configuration and realized I needed to convert my ladder diagram to FBD. Then, in online testing/simulation, I was able to use all the buttons and see them activate. Seems like the issue was caused by the [company_name] programming software. Thanks for the assistance.

Everything operates correctly now, even when the connection between the two modules is lost. However, I have a question: Is there a special flag that monitors the Ethernet connection? I've programmed the client and server [product_name] modules to control an input, but during operation, if power is lost to either the client or server, the controlled input line remains active—which shouldn’t happen. Does anyone have a solution for this? I use a Phoenix WDM fiber connection set between the modules because singlemode fiber was the only free option. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users face difficulties setting up two [product_name] devices in a master-master network configuration to ensure mutual signal exchange and failover detection. The primary challenge is programming reliable network communication with [product_name] programming software, alongside a lack of practical simulation tools and diagnostic feedback for digital inputs using basic button controls. Users also struggle to detect network or power losses across devices, sometimes resulting in unsafe states where input signals remain active despite disconnections.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the programming software to provide user-friendly simulation, transparent configuration of network inputs and outputs, and mechanisms for detecting device or connection failures. They also want example programs featuring button-based input simulation and easier access to diagnostic status indicators for network health.
pain_keywords: input state persistence after device/power loss
